title: A system upgrade changed the allocation rule
brief: Key account HomeMart receives only 60% of its ordered quantity of SKU R-250 (rice cooker) from the Antwerp DC, while smaller accounts get 100%. Find the root cause and an action plan.

evidence.content: R-250 available this week: 6,000 units. HomeMart ordered 5,000 and received 3,000; other accounts ordered 3,000 and received all 3,000.
The order-system upgrade on 3 Nov replaced the 'fair share by order week' allocation rule with 'first come, first served by order timestamp'.
HomeMart places one weekly order every Thursday at 18:00; smaller accounts order daily in the morning.

On-time delivery 98.1%; damages 0.2%; average truck fill 87%; 412 shipments; 9 carriers; CO2 per pallet down 3%; detention hours 61; claims 4 (EUR 2,300); lane Antwerp-Rotterdam fill 91%; lane Antwerp-Lille fill 84%; lane Antwerp-Cologne fill 79%; fuel surcharge +1.2%; two near-miss incidents at the yard; new dock scheduling tool live 20 Oct; no capacity constraints reported; no delays on HomeMart deliveries.
Supply is sufficient; the supplier shipped full PO quantities.
HomeMart's contract has a 95% fill-rate SLA, with a penalty of 2% of invoice value for each week below target.

answer_key.root_cause: The 3 Nov order-system upgrade switched allocation to first-come-first-served by timestamp, so accounts that order daily in the morning consume stock before HomeMart's weekly Thursday-evening order.

remediation_rubric.criterion: Restore fair-share allocation or reserve stock for key accounts
Quantify SLA penalty exposure and inform the account team
Change control/testing for order-system rule changes
Check other accounts affected by the rule change

answer_key.notes: E4 is long and irrelevant; the cause needs inventory + demand evidence together.

registry.mechanism_opportunities: V2 saves cost on E4 (nobody needs it). Demand -> Inventory evidence must combine (V1 path).
registry.favoritism_notes: Favours V2 and V1; balanced by HO-03 (V2 risk) and HO-05 (D0 synthesis).
